effect_estimate.comment: Outcomes reflect confirmed latrine sales orders rather than verified installations (typical cancellation rates in iDE programs are 10-20%). Comparing PPI vs. IDPoor eligibility pathways is observational within the randomized village-level subsidy intervention.
effect_estimate.value: Offering a targeted 50% price subsidy increased the household-level predicted probability of latrine purchase among eligible treatment households by 31.3 percentage points over ineligible control households (marginal probability = 0.313, p = 0.00; reported in text as 31 percentage points), while eligible control (0.0132, p = 0.416) and ineligible treatment (0.0056, p = 0.860) households did not differ significantly from base. Overall sales conversion was 22% in treatment villages vs. 7% in control villages (p = 0.00; 437 total latrines sold: 326 treatment, 111 control), and 38% among subsidy-eligible vs. 6% among ineligible households within treatment villages (p = 0.00; vs. 8% and 6% in control villages, p = 0.32). At the village level (N = 30 villages), offering subsidies increased overall closing rates by 23 percentage points (p = 0.00) and purchase rates among subsidy-qualifying households by 32 percentage points (p = 0.00): +37 percentage points among Poverty Probability Index (PPI)-qualifying households (p = 0.00) and +26 percentage points among IDPoor-qualifying households (p = 0.03). Household-level climate vulnerability increased purchase probability by an additional 10 percentage points when offered a subsidy (p = 0.00), with no evidence of market distortion among ineligible households (only 3 of 2,352 non-purchasers reported waiting for a subsidy). Programmatic cost per latrine sold was USD 224.22 in treatment vs. USD 602.07 in control (overall USD 320.20).

mechanism_certainty.comment: Cluster-randomized controlled trial directly randomizing the targeted sanitation subsidy mechanism across 30 villages (15 treatment, 15 control). Minor post-randomization identification imbalance is noted in Limitations (52% vs. 45% overall eligibility, p = 0.00, driven by a 5 percentage point higher share of IDPoor households identified with village authority assistance in treatment villages, while PPI qualification did not differ significantly) and outcomes measure orders rather than completed installations.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines a two-layer subsidy eligibility mechanism combining government IDPoor status with a 10-question Poverty Probability Index (PPI) and commune/household climate-vulnerability hardship thresholds to grant a 50% latrine price discount, alongside door-to-door screening procedures, M&E verification spot checks, village authority assistance in household identification, and street-level sales agent understanding/discretion.

sample_size.comment: 1,598 duplicate visit entries (36 resulting in a sale) were dropped from the original dataset prior to calculating closing rates, yielding 2,821 unique household sales presentations across 30 villages (437 total latrines sold and 2,352 non-purchasing households queried on reasons for non-purchase). Minimum power calculation required 26 villages with 100 households per village (2,600 households).

study_design.comment: Treatment (50% targeted latrine price subsidy for households meeting IDPoor or PPI/climate-vulnerability thresholds vs. retail-price-only sales pitches) was cluster-randomized at the village level stratified by commune climate vulnerability, analyzed via village-level OLS and household-level village-clustered logistic regressions, alongside thematic content analysis of 13 stakeholder interviews and programmatic cost-effectiveness modeling.
